question: Should Discord Activity support continue from this older core-path branch, move to the newer broader Activity PR, or restart as a Canvas-plugin-owned design with a fail-closed Activity auth model?
rationale: The unresolved choice crosses plugin ownership, Gateway authorization, token transport, operator config shape, and overlapping open PRs, so automation can identify blockers but should not choose the permanent security boundary.

options.title: Restart under Canvas plugin auth
options.body: Port the useful launch-button and A2UI ideas to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require Activity credentials or a verifiable exchange, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof.

options.title: Use the newer Activity PR after repair
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/65205 as the working branch only after its similar merge-state, security, compatibility, and proof blockers are resolved.

options.title: Pause Discord Activities
options.body: Keep Activity support out of core until maintainers settle whether this belongs in bundled plugins, an external package, or a narrower Discord-only API.

recommendation.title: Restart under Canvas plugin auth
recommendation.body: Port the useful launch-button and A2UI ideas to `extensions/canvas` and `extensions/discord`, require Activity credentials or a verifiable exchange, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking choice is mainly about Gateway auth, Canvas plugin config migration, and public config ownership, where the current-main history points most strongly to steipete.
